description: Prompt-cleaning vectors shared by the Python and Node SDKs. Generated by packages/descriptors/build_content_vectors.py; do not edit by hand.

definitions.case: Clean `input` under `policy` (a name in `policies`, or the policy itself) with the content block of the `provider` descriptor (none when null). Expect `output`, exactly `counts` (masked occurrences per detector id or custom:LABEL), exactly `blocked` (when not empty, the call is blocked and no output is stated) and `attachments`. `error: policy` means the policy itself must be refused. Every output must be a fixed point: cleaning it again changes nothing and counts nothing.
definitions.$concat: Anywhere in this file, an object whose only key is `$concat` stands for the string made by joining its parts, where a part {repeat, times} is `repeat` written `times` times. Secret-shaped strings are stored split this way so that no tracked file holds a whole key or token.
definitions.walk: Object keys are visited in RFC 8785 order (UTF-16 code units), arrays in order; placeholders are numbered in that order, then by position.
definitions.challenge: response = sha256(token + "\n" + the cleaned inputs joined by "\n"), each input cleaned on its own under the reference policy.
definitions.policy_digest: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the policy document.
definitions.positives: A value one catalogue detector takes whole, between `lead` and `trail` (the words a detector may need nearby). Both suites put each in generated contexts (prefixes, line prefixes, escaped newlines, suffixes, values lengthened past the engine's bounds, a private key cut before its END line) under a policy enabling that detector alone, and hold that whenever the detector counts something, no run of 4 characters of the value is left in the output: a value is taken whole or not at all.
